Priors for bayome models

Source: R/prior.R
bm_prior.Rd

Collects the priors used by bayome. Precisions of random effects and of ordered() random walks get penalised-complexity (PC) priors, set so that P(sd > u) = alpha. Fixed effects get Gaussian priors with mean 0.

Usage

bm_prior(
  random = c(1, 0.01),
  ordered = c(1, 0.01),
  strata_log_prec = -10,
  fixed_sd_prevalence = 2.5,
  fixed_sd_abundance = 10,
  adjustment_sd = 2.5
)

Arguments

random

PC prior for random-effect standard deviations, as c(u, alpha).

ordered

PC prior for the standard deviation of the rw1 effect used for ordered() variables, as c(u, alpha).

strata_log_prec

Fixed log-precision for strata() effects. A very small precision (large variance) makes each stratum act as its own free intercept, which mimics conditioning on the strata.

fixed_sd_prevalence

Prior standard deviation of the fixed effects (log-odds scale) in the prevalence model. The default, 2.5, is weakly informative for standardised covariates and keeps estimates finite under complete separation (for example a feature present in every case).

fixed_sd_abundance

Prior standard deviation of the fixed effects (log2 abundance scale) in the abundance model.

adjustment_sd

Prior standard deviation of the effect of each adjustment covariate on each feature (the covariates that are not the exposure of bayome() with shrinkage = "joint"), in both parts: log-odds for prevalence, log2 for abundance. These effects are not shared across features, so the prior is fixed; the default, 2.5, is weakly informative for standardised covariates.

Value

An object of class bm_prior: a list with hyper (the hyper lists passed to INLA's f()) and fixed (prior precisions of the fixed effects for the prevalence and abundance parts, and of the per-feature adjustment effects).

Examples

bm_prior(random = c(0.5, 0.01))
#> $hyper
#> $hyper$random
#> $hyper$random$prec
#> $hyper$random$prec$prior
#> [1] "pc.prec"
#> 
#> $hyper$random$prec$param
#> [1] 0.50 0.01
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> $hyper$ordered
#> $hyper$ordered$prec
#> $hyper$ordered$prec$prior
#> [1] "pc.prec"
#> 
#> $hyper$ordered$prec$param
#> [1] 1.00 0.01
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> $hyper$strata
#> $hyper$strata$prec
#> $hyper$strata$prec$initial
#> [1] -10
#> 
#> $hyper$strata$prec$fixed
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> 
#> $fixed
#> $fixed$prevalence
#> [1] 0.16
#> 
#> $fixed$abundance
#> [1] 0.01
#> 
#> $fixed$adjustment
#> [1] 0.16
#> 
#> 
#> attr(,"class")
#> [1] "bm_prior"
